title: BostonHacks 2026
organizer_blurb: Student-run, MLH-affiliated hackathon hosted at Boston University.
summary: A 24-hour weekend hackathon at BU's George Sherman Union, open to college students from any school. A short walk or T ride from Suffolk.
description: 24-hour event where students form teams and build projects, with workshops, sponsor recruiters and prizes (past prize list includes cameras, record players and monitors). You can register solo and find a team at the event. Food, swag and workspace are provided at no cost. Organizers state there is no travel reimbursement this year. Bring a laptop, charger and any hardware you want to hack with. Follows the MLH Code of Conduct.
location: George Sherman Union, Boston University, Boston, MA
dates_note: Runs Saturday Nov 21 to Sunday Nov 22, ending at noon on day two. Apply by Oct 28.
eligibility: All college students, undergraduate or graduate, from any background or school worldwide.

title: HackHarvard 2026: Hack to the Moon
organizer_blurb: Harvard's student-run collegiate hackathon held each fall in Cambridge.
summary: Harvard's fall hackathon for undergraduates, themed "Hack to the Moon" this year. Teams may mix schools and experience levels.
description: Weekend hackathon at Harvard with sponsor prize tracks. Listed sponsor prizes include $5,000 in credits, a $2,000 cash team prize plus per-member credits, Apple Store credit and gift cards; prizes go to each team member unless stated otherwise. Travel reimbursement and financial aid are limited and not guaranteed; selected participants are contacted separately. Applications for 2026 are closed, so treat this as a marker for the 2027 cycle.
dates_note: 2026 edition runs Oct 16–18; applications are closed. Watch for the 2027 cycle, likely opening in late summer.
pay: Free; limited travel reimbursement, not guaranteed
eligibility: Undergraduate students; teams can include students from different schools and experience levels.

title: HackMIT 2027
organizer_blurb: MIT student group running one of the largest undergraduate hackathons in the world.
summary: A 24-hour hackathon at MIT that brings over 1,000 undergraduates to campus each fall. No prior experience required.
description: 24-hour weekend hackathon on MIT's campus (check-in at Kresge Oval in 2026). Teams of up to 4, formed before or at the event. Admission is free and includes mentors, workshops, food and swag. Prizes in 2026: three general prizes, a beginner prize and four track prizes, plus mini-event raffles. Every attendee is eligible for travel reimbursement up to a regional cap, but only if they submit a complete project and follow the travel policy. An optional admissions puzzle exists; you still need to fill out an application.
dates_note: 2027 dates not announced. The 2026 edition ran Sept 19–20, with applications open in early June and closing in early July.
pay: Free; travel reimbursement up to a regional cap
eligibility: Undergraduates enrolled in a degree-seeking program (or MIT M.Eng students), 18 or older by the event date. High school students are not eligible. Student status is checked for the fall of the event year. Teams of up to 4.

title: HackBeanpot 2027
organizer_blurb: Boston nonprofit, founded in part by Northeastern students, that runs an annual undergraduate hackathon.
summary: An annual, beginner-friendly undergraduate hackathon in Boston held over a February weekend.
description: Weekend hackathon running Friday evening to early Sunday afternoon, with mentors, beginner workshops and guest speakers. Teams can be formed in the application or on day one, with team formation activities for solo hackers. Prizes are awarded by category. The 2026 edition did not offer travel reimbursement or overnight accommodations. Sign up for the newsletter on the site to hear when 2027 applications open.
dates_note: 2027 dates not announced. The 2026 edition ran Feb 13–15; applications closed before the event.
eligibility: Undergraduate students at an accredited college or university.

title: MIT Reality Hack 2027
organizer_blurb: Organizers of an annual mixed reality and spatial computing hackathon held at MIT.
summary: A multi-day XR, AR/VR and spatial computing hackathon at MIT with participants from around the world. Good fit for hardware and immersive-tech builders.
description: Multi-day in-person event at MIT (the 2026 edition ran five days, Jan 22–26). Individuals apply; accepted participants form teams through a team formation process. No fee to apply or participate. Participants arrange their own travel and lodging; travel support was undecided for 2026 and shared only with accepted participants. Meals provided for most of the event. Sponsor tracks and prizes are listed on the site's yearly prizes page. No remote option for the MIT event.
dates_note: Site says the next edition is in January 2027; exact dates not posted. The 2026 edition ran Jan 22–26, with application decisions by late December.
eligibility: Open to participants of all backgrounds and skill levels worldwide; the site lists no student or age requirement.

title: MIT iQuHACK 2027
organizer_blurb: MIT student-run quantum computing hackathon, now in its eighth year.
summary: MIT's quantum computing hackathon, with an in-person component on campus and separate in-person and remote application forms.
description: Weekend hackathon focused on quantum computing challenges, aimed at students and experts plus anyone keen to learn the field. The site offers separate in-person and remote application forms. Team size, prizes and travel support are not stated on the main page; check the site's FAQ before applying.
dates_note: Jan 29–31, 2027. Apply by Nov 18, 2026.
eligibility: Not stated on the main page; the event describes itself as serving students and experts as well as newcomers interested in quantum.

title: JumboHack Spring 2027
organizer_blurb: Tufts University's student-run computer science hackathon.
summary: Tufts' student-run hackathon in Medford/Somerville, which drew 300+ students from 25+ universities in 2025.
description: Weekend hackathon at Tufts' Joyce Cummings Center. The 2025 edition ran 48 hours with five tracks: general, a beginner track, emerging tech, sustainability and education. The top 2025 team won a $500 prize; other winners received tech gadgets. The site currently says Spring 2027 and offers a sign-up to be notified when registration opens.
dates_note: Spring 2027; exact dates and registration not announced. The 2025 edition ran Feb 22–23.
eligibility: Not stated on the current site; past editions drew students from many universities and included a beginner track.

title: HackPrinceton Fall 2026
organizer_blurb: Princeton University's student-run hackathon, held each fall and spring.
summary: A 36-hour in-person hackathon at Princeton for undergraduate and graduate students from any college.
description: 36 hours of hacking at Princeton's Julis Romo Rabinowitz Building. Teams of up to four; you do not need a team to apply. Free to apply and attend. More than $15K in prizes. Some admitted hackers may get a partial travel stipend, not guaranteed. Fall 2026 applications closed Sept 28; HackPrinceton also runs a spring edition.
dates_note: Nov 13–15, 2026. Applications closed Sept 28; watch for the spring edition.
pay: Free; $15K+ prizes; partial travel stipends for some
eligibility: Students matriculated in an undergraduate or graduate program at any college or university; no separate age minimum. Teams of up to 4.

title: Cal Hacks 13.0
organizer_blurb: UC Berkeley student group behind one of the largest collegiate hackathons, held in San Francisco.
summary: The 13th Cal Hacks, a large collegiate hackathon in San Francisco presented by Anthropic and other sponsors.
description: Weekend hackathon at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco, presented by Anthropic, Annapurna Labs, SpacetimeDB and Hyphenate. Teams of 2–4 are required. More than $126K in listed prizes: first overall includes $3,600 cash plus a laptop per member, along with category prizes for beginner, hardware, robotics, social impact and solo hacks, plus sponsor tracks such as MLH's Best Use of Gemini API. Only accepted, checked-in hackers can submit; projects are pitched live to judges.
dates_note: Oct 23–25, 2026. Admission is by prior acceptance; check calhacks.io for the 2027 cycle.
eligibility: College students only, 18+, in teams of 2–4. Only accepted, checked-in hackers can submit.

title: TreeHacks 2027
organizer_blurb: Stanford's student-run hackathon, now in its 13th year.
summary: A 36-hour hackathon on Stanford's campus, open to any enrolled college student worldwide, with flights, food and lodging covered.
description: 36-hour in-person hackathon at Stanford. Free for admitted hackers. Flights are covered up to regional caps, and food and lodging are provided. More than $1M in prizes listed. Teams can be formed at the event through a team-matching platform. Apply through the site; Stanford students get priority if they apply by a priority deadline.
dates_note: Feb 12–14, 2027. Application deadline not posted.
pay: Free; flights covered up to regional caps; $1M+ prizes
eligibility: Any enrolled college student (undergraduate or graduate) worldwide who agrees to the Code of Conduct.

title: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
organizer_blurb: Microsoft's long-running global student startup and technology competition.
summary: Microsoft's global student startup competition: teams of up to four students build an AI-powered product with Microsoft AI and pitch it online, with top teams advancing to a World Championship. The 2027 edition is listed as coming soon.
description: Student founder teams build an AI-powered product that uses at least two Microsoft AI services, aimed at one of five categories (Education, Financial Services, Health and Life Sciences, Retail and Consumer Goods, Cybersecurity) or a challenge of their own. Teams choose a path when they submit their MVP. Launch is for early-stage teams with no dilutive funding and at most $100,000 in non-dilutive funding; its winner is announced after the semifinals. Scale is for startups with users, revenue or capital and no more than $5M in combined funding; its top three teams reach the World Championship. MVP entries are a pitch deck, recorded pitch and demo video, all in English. Semifinalists get the Builder Series of training and mentorship from Microsoft experts. As of Oct 18, 2026 the homepage says Imagine Cup 2027 is coming soon, while the 2027 competition page already shows a Register Now button. 2027 rules, dates and prizes are not published yet (the rules link still opens the 2026 rules), so the details here come from the 2026 cycle.
dates_note: No 2027 dates are posted: the homepage says Coming Soon and the 2027 page has a Register Now button but no deadlines. For reference, the 2026 cycle took MVP submissions Sep 30, 2025 – Jan 9, 2026, ran Semifinals Feb 10 – Apr 7, 2026, and held the World Championship in April–May 2026.
eligibility: 2027 rules not posted yet. In the 2026 cycle: at least 18 as of Sep 30, 2025; enrolled at an accredited high school, college or university (home schools count) at any time between Sep 30, 2025 and May 31, 2026; not a resident of Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Sudan, Syria, Russia or Crimea, or a country barred by U.S. export rules. Teams of 1–4 students, all registered on the Imagine Cup site, who may come from different schools and countries. Past world champions cannot re-enter.
prizes: 2027 prizes not posted yet. 2026 cycle: Scale World Champion $100,000 plus a mentoring session with Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella; Launch winner $50,000; cash split equally among team members; some winners and finalists may attend Microsoft Build in person.
provided: Up to $5,000 in Azure credits after registering (per the 2027 page). In the 2026 cycle: access to Microsoft AI services, Microsoft Learn Student Hub training, live workshops with Microsoft MVPs before the MVP deadline, and Builder Series training and mentorship for semifinalists.

title: Google DeepMind Gemini 3 Hackathon
organizer_blurb: Google's AI research lab, which runs recurring online developer competitions for the Gemini API.
summary: Google's most recent global online Gemini API hackathon, with a $100,000 prize pool. Listed as a recurring program to watch; no new Google edition is open right now.
description: Online competition to build a new application using the Gemini 3 API, with no category restrictions (games, productivity tools, scientific analyzers, robotics controllers and so on). Only new projects were allowed. $100,000 prize pool plus interviews with Google's AI Futures Fund team. Open to beginners and experienced developers. Google ran several similar Gemini challenges on Devpost through 2026; watch Devpost and ai.google.dev for the next one.
dates_note: No current Google edition is open. The last Gemini 3 Hackathon ran Dec 17, 2025 – Feb 9, 2026; Google has run Gemini challenges on Devpost several times a year.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in your country of residence; some countries and territories excluded.

title: OpenAI Build Week Challenge
organizer_blurb: AI research and product company behind ChatGPT and Codex.
summary: OpenAI's global online build challenge for developers, creators, founders and students building with Codex. Listed as a program to watch; the 2026 edition has ended.
description: A week of live sessions, 40+ community events and a project challenge built around Codex. Participants submitted projects to the Build Week Challenge, and winners were announced on the OpenAI Developers Blog. Past winning projects covered veterinary care, speech accessibility and spatial audio. OpenAI has not announced another edition, so check OpenAI's developer channels for the next one.
dates_note: No current OpenAI hackathon is open. The 2026 Build Week started July 13 and winners were announced Aug 26; no future edition announced.
eligibility: Not stated on the page read; the challenge invited developers, creators, founders and students.

title: PayPal AI Hackathon
organizer_blurb: Global payments company opening its developer platform to AI-driven projects.
summary: A global online hackathon to build anything that meaningfully uses both PayPal's developer platform and AI. Open to individuals or teams.
description: No set tracks or problem statements: build an agent, app, automation, payment experience or business tool that integrates at least one PayPal API or SDK (using the free sandbox) and meaningfully uses AI. You can start something new or substantially extend an existing project, and sponsor tools are optional. Prizes total about $67.5K in cash, with overall and special awards for creativity, impact and execution. Kickoff webinars ran in early October. A working prototype or proof of concept is required.
dates_note: Submissions due Nov 12, 2026 at 12:00 pm PT.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in your country of residence; most countries eligible, with standard exceptions. Individuals or teams.

title: Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026
organizer_blurb: Meta's developer program for building apps on Meta Quest and Meta VR devices.
summary: An eight-week online competition to build hands-first VR experiences for Meta Quest and Meta VR Glasses, with $1M in cash prizes.
description: Members of Meta's Start developer program build Entertainment, Gaming or Productivity experiences for Meta VR devices, focused on hand-tracking interaction. Top prizes reach $100,000 per track winner, plus special craft awards, out of $1M total. Includes mentor programming and quickstart tutorials for Unity, Unreal, Android and the Immersive Web SDK. Joining the Start program is free and the application takes about five minutes.
dates_note: Submissions due Nov 18, 2026 at 12:00 pm PT.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in your country of residence and a member of Meta's Start program (you can apply to join); some countries excluded.

title: Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon
organizer_blurb: Meta's AI team, co-hosting this event with Cerebral Valley, an AI developer community that runs hackathons and builder events.
summary: A ten-day online hackathon building with Meta's newest AI models, with $1M in cash prizes split between an indie developer track and a startup track. Entry is by application, and applications close Oct 25.
description: Accepted participants spend ten days building with Meta's models: the Muse Spark series, Muse Image and SAM 3.1 through the Meta Model API, Meta's open-weights models, and the Muse Code agentic coding tool. Projects should fit one of two themes: bringing the models into a field you know firsthand, or pushing into areas like robotics, manufacturing, energy or materials. Each project goes in one track. The indie developer track is for individual builders and students and is judged on creativity, technical ambition and whether the project works; the startup track is for technical founders and is judged on execution and production readiness. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, weighting equally how clear and feasible your project idea is and the technical skill shown in an AI project you describe (GitHub or LinkedIn links help but are optional). Acceptance is capped at 20,000 people and the form can close early once the cap is hit, so apply early. Official rules will be posted before the Oct 26 kickoff. Projects are submitted through Cerebral Valley's portal.
dates_note: Applications opened Oct 13 at 9:00 AM ET and close Oct 25 at 11:59 PM ET, or sooner if all 20,000 spots fill; acceptance emails go out by 9:00 AM ET Oct 26. Kickoff livestream Oct 26; workshops and Discord office hours through Nov 4; submissions due Nov 4 at 9:00 PM ET. Judging Nov 4–8, live finals and winners Nov 9, bonus prizes announced around Nov 10. Meta says dates may change.
eligibility: Must apply and be accepted (cap of 20,000). At least 18 and the age of majority where you live. Open worldwide except where local law prohibits taking part or receiving a prize; anyone targeted by U.S., EU, UN or UK sanctions or export controls, acting for such a party, or located in Belarus, China, Russia, Ukraine, Syria, Cuba, North Korea, Iran or the Crimea, Donetsk and Luhansk regions is not eligible. Employees, contractors and interns of Meta and Cerebral Valley, government-affiliated individuals, and their immediate family and household members are excluded. One track per participant: indie track for individual builders and students (teams up to four), startup track for technical founders building a product.
team_size: Indie track: solo or teams up to 4; startup track: founder teams (size not stated)
prizes: $1,000,000 total. Indie developer track $400,000: 1st $150,000, 2nd $100,000, 3rd $75,000, 4th $50,000, 5th $25,000. Startup track $550,000, listed as 1st $250,000 and 2nd $150,000. Up to $50,000 in bonus awards (e.g. community vote, most viral project).
provided: $150 in Meta Model API credits for each accepted participant. For select participants: $100 in Baseten credits with 2M TPM rate limits, $100 in Modal credits, and $25 in Fireworks credits. Kickoff livestream, live workshops from Meta and partners, and office hours on Discord.

title: Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon
organizer_blurb: Nebius is an AI cloud company whose Token Factory service hosts open-source models, including NVIDIA's, for developers to call.
summary: An online Devpost hackathon to build an AI app or agent that runs on Nebius and uses an NVIDIA open-source model, with $50,000+ in prizes. Submissions close Oct 30.
description: Build a working AI project that makes runtime calls to Nebius Token Factory (or runs on Nebius AI Cloud) and uses at least one NVIDIA open-source model such as Nemotron, GR00T, Cosmos or Sonic. Every project goes in one of four tracks: Coding and Agentic Engineering (agents that write, run and test code), Best Apps and Agents, Personal AI (a private, always-on assistant with memory and tools), or Physical AI (robotics, IoT and edge devices; simulation tools like Isaac Sim are allowed). A submission needs a working demo link, a public repo with an open-source license and a README, a public YouTube demo under three minutes, and written feedback on the Nebius and NVIDIA tools you used. Older projects count only if significantly updated during the submission period. Judges score technical implementation, design, potential impact and quality of the idea equally. Nebius and Tavily also ran in-person Builders & Brews meetups in 20 cities, including Boston on Oct 2; the $500 City Winner awards are for entrants tied to those events. More than 24,000 people had joined by Oct 18.
dates_note: Submission period runs Aug 26 (9:00 AM PT) to Oct 30, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT (1:00 PM ET); you can join on Devpost any time before the deadline, and opens_on is the official submission-period start. Judging Dec 1–15, 2026; winners announced on or around Jan 11, 2027. A live judges' session, Will It Ship, is on Oct 20 at 12:00 PM ET.
eligibility: At least the age of majority where you live at the time of entry. Individuals, teams and organizations can enter; teams and organizations name one representative to submit. Not open to residents of Brazil, Quebec, Russia, Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea or other OFAC-sanctioned countries, or to staff of Nebius, Devpost and others running the hackathon, judges or companies that employ a judge, and the immediate family and household members of those involved. Some countries cannot yet sign up for Nebius Token Factory billing even though they are eligible.
team_size: Solo, a team of any size, or an organization (no maximum)
prizes: $50,000+ total. Grand Prize $20,000, 2nd $10,000, 3rd $6,000; an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano for each of the 4 track winners; Best Use of Tavily $3,000; 20 City Winner awards of $500; 10 Most Valuable Feedback awards of $100 plus an NVIDIA swag pack. A project can win one overall award, or one track award plus one bonus award.
provided: $25 in Nebius Token Factory credits through the hackathon credits form, plus another $25 and Tavily and Nebius Academy credits by joining the free Nebius Builders Program (which also gives office hours). Recorded live build sessions, Discord support, and in-person Builders & Brews meetups with mentors, workshops and extra credits in participating cities.

title: MLH Global Hack Week: Builders Week
organizer_blurb: The official student hackathon league, which runs Global Hack Week as a free monthly online event.
summary: A free, week-long online MLH event with beginner-friendly sessions and challenges focused on building. A good first hackathon for new club members.
description: Global Hack Week runs one week each month with live sessions, daily challenges, a Discord community and streamed workshops. Builders Week is themed around creating, with "builder" defined broadly. Free for anyone. The next week, Open Source Week, runs Dec 4–10, 2026.
dates_note: Nov 6–12, 2026. Next is Open Source Week, Dec 4–10, 2026; MLH runs a new week roughly every month.
eligibility: Open to anyone, anywhere, from beginners to experienced hackers.

title: Hackachusetts 2026
organizer_blurb: A private-sector coalition of Massachusetts AI founders, operators, students and investors that runs community events and programs.
summary: A one-day statewide AI hackathon at nine Massachusetts campuses, open to any student enrolled in Massachusetts. Suffolk students can pick a nearby site such as Northeastern, BU or UMass Boston.
description: Hackachusetts runs on Saturday, October 24, 2026 from 8 AM to 8 PM at nine host sites: MIT and The Engine, Harvard, Boston College, Boston University, Northeastern, UMass Amherst, UMass Lowell, UMass Boston, and Babson with The Generator. You do not have to attend the host school; you pick a campus when you register through the SundAI event page. There are four challenge tracks: biotech and healthcare, robotics and hardware, energy and climate tech, and civic action. Breakfast, lunch and dinner are served at every site, and Amazon's Kiro team gives participants 2,000 free Kiro credits in person; vibe-coded projects must be submitted with Kiro. About 50 finalists are notified at midnight and pitch at a Sunday brunch at WHOOP headquarters on October 25 from 11 AM to 2 PM. Solo builders are allowed but teams are encouraged. The page does not state a registration deadline or a fee.
location: Nine Massachusetts campuses incl. Northeastern (Snell Engineering Center), BU, UMass Boston, Boston, MA
dates_note: Saturday, October 24, 8 AM to 8 PM at all sites. Finalist pitching and awards Sunday, October 25, 11 AM to 2 PM at WHOOP headquarters. Part of Tough Tech Week.
eligibility: Students enrolled anywhere in Massachusetts. A .edu email address is required to register and student IDs are checked at the event.
prizes: $30,000 total prize pool: first, second and third place in each of four tracks (12 winners), plus $5,000 in prizes for remaining participants in each track; finalists receive WHOOP straps.
provided: Breakfast, lunch and dinner at all nine sites; 2,000 free Kiro credits per student.

title: DS+X Hackathon 2026
organizer_blurb: BU Spark! is Boston University's computing and data sciences innovation and experiential learning lab.
summary: A two-day data science hackathon at BU's Faculty of Computing & Data Sciences, and the BU site of Hackachusetts. It welcomes students who are not expert data scientists and pays cash prizes.
description: DS+X stands for Data Science plus X, where X is any field you care about, such as health, art or college life. It runs October 24 to 25, 2026 at the BU Center for Computing & Data Sciences and is an official Hackachusetts site, so projects may also be eligible for Hackachusetts recognition. Tracks are CollegeHack (challenges from BU IS&T), Health+BioTech Hack, ArtHack and OpenHack. Teams submit a GitHub repo with a README, slides and a demo video. Registering on Devpost is not enough; you must also fill out the Airtable application linked on the page. Devpost lists the event as open to people above the legal age of majority, US only. The page does not state a fee or team size.
location: BU Center for Computing & Data Sciences, 665 Commonwealth Ave, Boston, MA
dates_note: Saturday and Sunday, October 24 to 25, 2026. Devpost shows submissions as opening soon.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in country of residence; US only (per Devpost). Aimed at students.
prizes: $5,500+ in cash: Top Overall $1,000; track prizes for Health & BioTech, Art & Design and College Hack ($250 to $750); Best First-Time Hacker $500; Best First-Year Hacker $500; plus Lovable credits and BU Libraries prizes.

title: Code Metal Forge Hackathon 2026: Operation Lost and Found
organizer_blurb: Code Metal is a Boston company building AI and edge computing systems for mission-critical environments.
summary: A free, in-person search-and-rescue hardware and AI hackathon in downtown Boston, a short walk from Suffolk. University participants on the winning team get an internship interview at Code Metal.
description: The Forge Hackathon runs November 6 to 8, 2026 at BASE-X, 60 State Street in Boston, and is sponsored by U.S. Special Operations Command. Teams of up to four build prototypes that help responders locate, detect and reach isolated people when GPS, cell networks or other infrastructure fail. Hackers get access to embedded computing boards, software-defined radios, thermal and environmental sensors, and mentors from defense, deep tech and Code Metal. Participation is free and by application, reviewed on a rolling basis; solo applicants are matched with a team on Saturday morning. Meals are served from the Friday reception through Sunday awards, and the venue stays open overnight. Participants must get themselves to the event.
location: BASE-X, 60 State Street, Suite 1400, Boston, MA
dates_note: Friday, November 6 reception from 5 PM; build starts Saturday, November 7 at 10 AM; submissions close Sunday, November 8 at noon, with judging and awards that afternoon. The FAQ lists an application deadline of October 5, while the page still says applications are open on a rolling basis, so check before applying.
eligibility: Open by application to university teams and individual technologists. No other requirements stated on the page.
prizes: $18,000 prize pool: $10,000 first, $5,000 second, $3,000 third; winning team meets Code Metal leadership and university members get an internship interview.
provided: Breakfast, lunch, dinner, snacks and drinks all weekend; T-shirt, water bottle, sling backpack and challenge coin; embedded, radio and sensor hardware; mentors.

title: WHACK 2026: Wish upon a Whale
organizer_blurb: WHACK is Wellesley College's student-run hackathon, an MLH member event.
summary: A free weekend hackathon at Wellesley College, reachable from Boston by commuter rail. Open to any college student in a degree program.
description: WHACK 2026 takes place November 21 to 22, 2026 at Wellesley College, hosted in Tishman Commons of the Lulu Chow Wang Center, where there are also sleeping areas. It is open to all current college and university students enrolled in a degree-seeking program. You can apply solo or with a team of up to four, and there is a team-forming event on Friday evening. Registration, meals, snacks, swag and workshops are free. Organizers provide three meals on Saturday and breakfast and lunch on Sunday. Travel is not reimbursed. The detailed schedule and prizes are not yet posted.
location: Lulu Chow Wang Campus Center, Wellesley College, Wellesley, MA
dates_note: Saturday to Sunday, November 21 to 22, 2026, with a team-forming event Friday evening. The site schedule still shows times as TBD.
eligibility: All current college and university students enrolled in a degree-seeking program.
provided: Three meals Saturday, two meals Sunday, snacks, swag, workshops, sleeping area.

title: HackUMass XIV
organizer_blurb: HackUMass is UMass Amherst's student-run, MLH-member hackathon.
summary: A 36-hour hackathon at UMass Amherst with hardware to borrow and workshops for all levels. Open to any college student, including grad students.
description: HackUMass XIV runs November 13 to 15, 2026 at the Integrative Learning Center on the UMass Amherst campus. It is open to all college students, including graduate students, of any major. Applications are open through dashboard.hackumass.com. Teams of four or fewer are encouraged; larger teams are allowed but prizes are not guaranteed for members past four. Hardware such as Arduinos, Raspberry Pis and quadcopters is available, and there are workshops, mentors and a sponsor fair. Travel reimbursement was offered only to early-deadline applicants and that window has closed. Projects must start after the opening ceremony and at least one team member must be present for judging.
location: Integrative Learning Center, 650 N Pleasant St, Amherst, MA
dates_note: Friday to Sunday, November 13 to 15, 2026 (36 hours). Dates confirmed on the MLH 2027 season list. The XIV schedule is not yet published.
pay: Not stated on the page; travel reimbursement closed (early-deadline applicants only)
eligibility: All college students, including graduate students, regardless of major. Must follow the MLH and UMass codes of conduct.
provided: Meals and late-night snacks (per last year's schedule), hardware lending, workshops, mentors, sponsor swag.

title: Hack@Brown 2027
organizer_blurb: Hack@Brown is Brown University's student-run, MLH-member hackathon.
summary: Brown University's annual hackathon in Providence, about an hour from Boston by train. Applications are not open yet.
description: Hack@Brown 2027 is set for February 6 to 7, 2027, according to its site, which shows a coming-soon banner and a form to get notified when hacker applications open. The event follows the MLH Code of Conduct. The page does not yet list the venue, eligibility, cost, travel support, team size or prizes. The MLH 2027 season list shows the event as February 5 to 7 in Providence, RI.
dates_note: The event site says February 6 to 7, 2027; the MLH season list shows February 5 to 7, 2027 (likely including Friday check-in). Hacker applications are not open yet.
eligibility: Not stated on the page.

title: MIT Battlecode 2027
organizer_blurb: Battlecode is MIT's long-running programming competition where teams write AI bots for a real-time strategy game.
summary: A month-long AI programming competition run by MIT every January, with online play and a final tournament on the MIT campus. Non-MIT student teams can compete for prize money.
description: Battlecode runs each January. Teams write autonomous bot code for a new real-time strategy game revealed at kickoff, then compete in sprint, qualifier and final tournaments. In 2026 it ran January 5 to 31 with evening lectures at MIT streamed on YouTube, US and international qualifiers, a mini career fair, and a final tournament in MIT room 10-250. Anyone can participate; sprint tournament prizes are open to any team, while the remaining tournaments and prize money are limited to student teams, including non-MIT students. Sponsors in 2026 included Jane Street, Hudson River Trading, Citadel and D. E. Shaw. Registration is through play.battlecode.org.
location: MIT, Cambridge, MA (final tournament); online play
dates_note: 2027 dates are not announced yet; the site currently shows the 2026 season (January 5 to 31, 2026) and a call for 2027 sponsors. Expect a January 2027 start.
eligibility: Anyone can participate; most tournaments and prize money are limited to student teams, including non-MIT students.
prizes: More than $20,000 in prizes in 2026; 2027 prizes not posted.

title: GoatHacks 2027
organizer_blurb: GoatHacks, formerly Hack@WPI, is Worcester Polytechnic Institute's MLH-member hackathon run by its ACM student chapter.
summary: WPI's annual January hackathon in Worcester, open to university students 18 and older. Software and hardware projects are welcome.
description: GoatHacks is an overnight hackathon at WPI that supports both software and hardware projects and does not require coding experience. Hackers must be 18 or older and attend a college or university. Teams can have 1 to 5 people, and solo hacking is allowed. Food and refreshments are provided and the venue stays open overnight. The site still shows the January 2026 edition (January 16 to 18) and has not posted 2027 dates.
dates_note: 2027 dates not announced. The site still shows January 16 to 18, 2026; past editions ran on a mid-January weekend.
eligibility: Must be 18 or older and attending a college or university.
provided: Food and refreshments; venue open overnight.

title: YHack 2027
organizer_blurb: YHack is Yale University's flagship student-run hackathon.
summary: Yale's 24-hour hackathon in New Haven with large prize pools and travel reimbursement for East Coast students. The 2027 date is not out yet.
description: YHack brings 600+ college builders together for 24 hours of weekend hacking with hardware, technical workshops and recruiting events. It is free, teams are 1 to 4 people, and you do not need hackathon experience. Accepted participants could apply for travel reimbursement, with many East Coast travelers supported. The spring 2026 edition ran March 28 to 29, 2026 with tracks in societal impact, entertainment, personal AI agents, prediction markets and hardware, and listed 100k in prizes. The site now invites visitors to subscribe for YHack 2027 updates.
dates_note: 2027 dates not announced. The last edition ran Saturday to Sunday, March 28 to 29, 2026; the site has a subscribe form for 2027 updates.
pay: Free; travel reimbursement available to accepted participants (2026 policy)
eligibility: College students; all skill levels (stated as 600+ college builders).
provided: Meals, snacks, swag, sleeping area, hardware, workshops (2026).

title: SBUHacks 2026: Steel and Steam
organizer_blurb: The Stony Brook Computing Society is a student CS organization at Stony Brook University.
summary: A 36-hour MLH hackathon at Stony Brook University on Long Island this weekend. Open to students 18+ at any school.
description: SBUHacks 2026 runs October 23 to 25, 2026 at Stony Brook University, with events in the SAC Auditorium, Melville Library Central Reading Room and SAC Ballroom A. Check-in starts Friday at 6 PM and Devpost submissions are due Sunday at 9 AM. Organizers expect 300+ hackers. The schedule includes breakfast, lunch, dinner and snacks, plus workshops on cybersecurity, full-stack deployment with AI, GitHub Copilot, Google AI Studio, Arduino and REST APIs. Registration is through a form linked on the page; no deadline is listed.
location: Student Activities Center, Stony Brook University, Stony Brook, NY
dates_note: Friday 6 PM check-in to Sunday morning; submissions due Sunday, October 25 at 9 AM.
eligibility: Over 18 and enrolled at any level at a traditional or nontraditional institution, or graduated within the past year (80% of spots reserved for this group).
prizes: Over $3,000: Best Overall $1,000 cash, Apple Watch SE 3, Bambu Lab A1 Mini; Best Hardware Hack (NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano); Best Beginner Hack (AirPods Pro 3); Best UX/UI Hack; MLH tracks.

title: HackRPI 2026: In the Clouds
organizer_blurb: HackRPI is RPI's annual student-run hackathon, now in its 13th year.
summary: A free 24-hour hackathon at RPI in Troy, NY, open to college students and recent grads from any school. Beginners are welcome.
description: HackRPI 2026 runs Saturday and Sunday, November 7 to 8, 2026 at the Darrin Communications Center on the RPI campus. Teams of 1 to 4 build software, hardware or both around the theme In the Clouds. Check-in is 9 to 10 AM Saturday, hacking starts at 11 AM, and Devpost submissions are due at 9 AM Sunday, with the event ending around 3 PM. Attendance, food and swag are free. There is no travel reimbursement, but on-campus sleep rooms are available for those 18 and older. Registration goes through MLH. Workshops are led by professors, sponsors and students.
location: Darrin Communications Center, RPI, 51 College Ave, Troy, NY
dates_note: Saturday 9 AM check-in to Sunday about 3 PM. Projects due on Devpost at 9 AM Sunday.
eligibility: College and university students, high school students, and early-career people up to 3 years out of college; you do not need to attend RPI. Under-18s cannot use sleep rooms and under-17s need a 21+ chaperone. Devpost lists the hackathon as students only.
prizes: $3,550 in cash prizes listed on Devpost, plus physical prizes.
provided: Free food and swag, sleep rooms for 18+, workshops, mentors.

title: MakeCU 2026
organizer_blurb: MakeCU is Columbia University's student-run hardware hackathon.
summary: Columbia's weekend hardware hackathon in Manhattan, where student teams build working physical prototypes. Good for students into robotics, embedded systems or IoT.
description: MakeCU runs November 7 to 8, 2026 at Columbia University's Carleton Commons. Students from schools including Columbia, NYU, Harvard and Caltech build functional physical prototypes from scratch over the weekend. It includes technical workshops from industry, hands-on events, networking with corporate sponsors, and a project expo with judging for track prizes. The event drew over 80 student builders last year. Registration details, cost and eligibility are on the official site, which could not be read directly.
location: Carleton Commons, Columbia University, New York, NY
dates_note: Saturday to Sunday, November 7 to 8, 2026. Also on the MLH 2027 season list.
eligibility: Not stated on the page (described as a student hackathon).

title: NASA Space Apps Challenge NYC 2026
organizer: SWARM NYC with NYU (NASA Space Apps local event)
organizer_blurb: NASA Space Apps is a global hackathon funded by NASA's Science Mission Directorate, run locally by volunteer hosts.
summary: The New York City site of NASA's global Space Apps hackathon, held at NYU Tandon in Brooklyn. Teams use NASA's open data to tackle one of 14 challenges.
description: NASA Space Apps NYC runs November 13 to 15, 2026 at NYU Tandon, 6 MetroTech Center in Brooklyn. Teams pick from 14 global challenges built on NASA's free and open data, meet mentors, and present to local judges. The event brings together students and professionals from NYU Tandon, the NYU School of Professional Studies and the wider NYC tech community. You do not need to be a programmer, scientist or space expert. Registration is through the Space Apps site, with an in-person limit of 300. It is organized locally by SWARM NYC with NYU.
location: NYU Tandon, 6 MetroTech Center, Brooklyn, NY
dates_note: Friday, November 13 (doors open 4:30 PM, opening remarks 5 PM) through Sunday, November 15, 2026.
eligibility: Open to students and professionals; no programming or science background required. Other requirements not stated on the page.

title: NYC Environmental Agent-a-thon 2027
organizer_blurb: ProgramEarth is a public benefit corporation building open-source tools for reforestation and land restoration.
summary: A one-day student hackathon in New York City where teams build AI agents for environmental data used by public-sector agencies. Projects can continue with agency partners afterward.
description: The Agent-a-thon runs February 20, 2027 in New York City. Student teams build working AI agents, data visualizations or open-source tools for real environmental workflows, such as flood and wildfire risk, watershed monitoring and GIS dashboards, using sponsor APIs and public datasets. The day runs from 9 AM check-in and breakfast through a 12 to 5 PM build session, demos and a reception until 7 PM. Agency partners evaluate projects, and useful tools may be adopted after the event. The page says students from CUNY, SUNY, Columbia and Cornell take part. Applications are open through the Apply as a participant link; the page does not state a cost or venue.
dates_note: Saturday, February 20, 2027, 9 AM to 7 PM. Sponsor commitments close January 31, 2027; no participant deadline is posted.
eligibility: Described as a hackathon for students. No other requirements stated on the page.
provided: Breakfast and lunch, live captions, wheelchair access, quiet space, livestream.

title: HackHERS 2027
organizer_blurb: Rutgers Women in Computer Science (WiCS) is a student organization supporting women in computing at Rutgers.
summary: Rutgers' women-centric 24-hour hackathon in New Brunswick, NJ. People of all genders may attend.
description: HackHERS is Rutgers WiCS's annual 24-hour hackathon focused on closing the gender gap in tech, held at the College Avenue Student Center. The 2027 edition is set for February 27 to 28, 2027. It is beginner-friendly, with workshops, mentors, tech talks and social events throughout. Tracks have covered machine learning and data, healthcare and sustainability, games and AR/VR, and fintech. Since 2015 it has had more than 1,600 hackers and $26,000+ in prizes. Parts of the site, such as the schedule, still show last year's content.
location: College Avenue Student Center, Rutgers University, New Brunswick, NJ
dates_note: Saturday to Sunday, February 27 to 28, 2027 per the site header and MLH 2027 season list. Some site sections still show the 2026 schedule.
eligibility: Geared toward women; people of all genders may participate (see the site's rules on mixed-gender teams).

title: DeveloperWeek New York 2027 Hackathon
organizer_blurb: DevNetwork runs the DeveloperWeek conference series and related developer hackathons.
summary: A challenge-driven hackathon co-located with DeveloperWeek New York, with an online phase and an in-person finish at the Meadowlands Exposition Center in NJ. Students can compete online or on site.
description: The online phase runs May 31 to June 17, 2027 and the in-person portion and awards are June 15 to 17, 2027 at the Meadowlands Exposition Center in Secaucus, NJ. Teams form on Devpost and build web or mobile apps, either open-ended or for sponsor challenges. Round 1 judges score progress, concept and feasibility for the overall winner; in Round 2 sponsors pick their own challenge winners. The overall winner receives prizes valued at $12,500, including Amazon Echos and DevNetwork passes. Devpost lists entrants as anyone above the legal age of majority in most countries. The page does not state a cost for hackathon participants.
location: Meadowlands Exposition Center, Secaucus, NJ + Online
dates_note: Online May 31 to June 17, 2027; in person and awards June 15 to 17, 2027.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in country of residence; all countries except standard exceptions.
prizes: Overall winner: $12,500 value (Amazon Echos, DevNetwork all-access passes, newsletter feature); sponsor challenge prizes to be added.

title: Kiroween 2026
organizer_blurb: Kiro is an AI coding IDE and agent from Amazon Web Services.
summary: An online Halloween-themed hackathon from AWS's Kiro with $100,000 in cash prizes. Open worldwide to adults, beginner-friendly, solo or team.
description: Kiroween returns for 2026 with the same four theme categories as last year: Resurrection (bring dead tech back to life), Frankenstein (stitch unlikely technologies together), Skeleton Crew (a reusable code template shown in two apps) and Costume Contest (a polished, spooky interface). Registration is open now, but only new projects started during the submission period count, so do not start building before October 30. Full rules, judging criteria and prize breakdown are released when submissions open. You need a Kiro user ID or AWS account ID to register. You can enter alone or with a team.
dates_note: Submissions open Friday, October 30, 2026 and close Friday, December 4, 2026 at 2:00 PM Pacific.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in country of residence; all countries except standard exceptions.
prizes: $100,000 in cash; category breakdown released October 30.

title: Life After Code: GitLab Transcend Hackathon
organizer_blurb: GitLab is a DevSecOps platform company.
summary: An online hackathon to build AI agents and flows on GitLab Duo Agent Platform that automate code review, security, testing and deployment. Judges come from GitLab, Google and Anthropic.
description: Projects must use GitLab Duo Agent Platform features such as agents, flows or MCP clients to automate parts of the DevSecOps lifecycle after code is written. Path A is a new project built from scratch; Path B wraps automation around an existing MIT-licensed open-source project. Entrants choose a level of autonomy from assisted to supervised and beyond. Contributor onboarding takes about 24 hours for approval, so register early. Deploying on Google Cloud can earn up to 0.2 bonus points. Several countries and Quebec are excluded.
dates_note: Submission deadline Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC (9:00 AM EDT).
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in country of residence; excludes Brazil, China, Quebec, Russia and sanctioned regions.

title: Qloo Agentic Hackathon
organizer_blurb: Qloo is a cultural AI company whose taste graph API covers music, film, dining, fashion and travel.
summary: An online hackathon to build AI agents that use Qloo's taste API for culturally grounded recommendations. Top three finalists present on air to Jason Calacanis.
description: Build a working app that integrates the Qloo API and is an agentic tool, uses an agent framework, or adds Qloo to an existing agent. The project should do something an LLM alone could not, using Qloo's taste graph of 250M+ entities. The top three finalists appear on air on November 5 with Jason Calacanis, Cedric the Entertainer and Alex Elias, who pick the winner, and must be available for that appearance. Calacanis also says he will personally invest $25,000 in his favorite entry. API keys are available through Qloo's hackathon developer guide.
dates_note: Deadline Friday, October 30, 2026 at 11:45 PM EDT. Finalists present live on November 5.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in country of residence; all countries except standard exceptions.
prizes: $25,000 in cash, plus a possible $25,000 investment from Jason Calacanis in his favorite entry.

title: OpenCV AI Competition 2026, powered by AWS
organizer: OpenCV Foundation with Amazon Web Services
organizer_blurb: The OpenCV Foundation maintains OpenCV, the open-source computer vision library.
summary: An online computer vision competition: build an app that uses OpenCV 5 and runs on AWS. Final projects are due this weekend.
description: Every entry must use OpenCV 5 for substantive image or video analysis and run a meaningful component on AWS. The competition emphasizes physical AI and generative AI systems where vision drives decisions or actions. Two optional paths carry separate $1,000 awards: Best Use of COOL and Agentic Vision. The build phase ran August 26 to October 26; judging runs October 27 to November 9 and winners are announced November 10 on OpenCV Live. Any programming language or hardware is allowed.
dates_note: Final projects due Monday, October 26, 2026 at 11:59 PM Pacific (Devpost lists 11:45 PM PDT). Winners announced November 10.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in country of residence; all countries except standard exceptions.
prizes: $20,250 in cash, including $1,000 awards for Best Use of COOL and Agentic Vision.

title: Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon
organizer_blurb: Amazon Developer supports third-party developers building for Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring and other Amazon devices and services.
summary: An online hackathon to build for Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring or the Bee wearable, with $138,000 in cash. It closes Friday, so only for students who already have a project underway.
description: Pick a primary track (Fire TV, Alexa+, Bee or Ring) and submit a working demo, code repo and product feedback. Alexa+ entries can be a self-hosted MCP server, an Agent Skill, or a simulated Alexa+ web app; Ring entries do not need a physical device. Mini challenges, such as AWS Builder, stack on the same project, but each project can win only one track prize and one mini challenge prize. Track winners also get a 1:1 meeting with the Amazon Developer team. Over 61,000 people have registered.
dates_note: Deadline Friday, October 23, 2026 at 12:00 PM Pacific.
eligibility: Above the legal age of majority in country of residence; all countries except standard exceptions.
prizes: $138,000 in cash (page cites $190K total value including AWS credits).

title: DeveloperWeek 2027 Hackathon

title: MLH Global Hack Week: Open Source Week
organizer_blurb: Major League Hacking is the official student hackathon league and runs events and programs for student developers.
summary: A free week of online open-source challenges, livestreams and workshops from MLH. Good for students who want their first open-source contributions.
description: Open Source Week is MLH's December Global Hack Week, running December 4 to 10, 2026. Global Hack Weeks are free online events where participants follow live challenges, attend sessions, build portfolio projects and connect with the MLH community on Discord. This edition focuses on all things open source. Registration is through the Global Hack Week site.
dates_note: Friday, December 4 through Thursday, December 10, 2026.

title: Vultr: Agent Rush Hackathon
organizer_blurb: lablab.ai runs online and hybrid AI hackathons with tech sponsors.
summary: A six-day online AI agents hackathon on Vultr cloud, with an optional on-site finale in Salt Lake City. Every participant gets $200 in Vultr credits.
description: Teams build a web-based AI agent on Vultr infrastructure in one of two challenges: Blast Radius Zero, an agent that writes and runs code or drives a browser inside an isolated sandbox, or Powering the Future of Work, an enterprise workflow app for areas like finance, HR or support. Challenge 1 must use Vultr Serverless Inference for LLM calls; Vultr GPUs are not available. The online build runs November 3 to 8, 2026, and approved teams may showcase on site in Salt Lake City on November 8, with travel and lodging not covered. Submissions must be original.

dates_note: Online build November 3 to 8, 2026; on-site phase November 8 for approved teams.
pay: Free; travel to on-site phase not covered
eligibility: Not stated on the page.
prizes: $9,000 cash ($5,000 / $3,000 / $1,000) plus $5,000 in Vultr credits; on-site raffle.
provided: $200 in free Vultr credits per participant.

title: United Hacks V8
organizer_blurb: Hack United is a student-run nonprofit that organizes free online hackathons for students.
summary: A free, beginner-friendly online weekend hackathon run by students for students. A low-pressure way to ship a first project over winter break.
description: United Hacks V8 runs January 8 to 10, 2027 online, with livestreams and workshops through its Discord server. There is a general track open to any topic and a theme track announced at the opening ceremony. Submissions need a public repo, a 2 to 5 minute demo video and a written description on Devpost, and all code must be written during the event. Projects cannot be submitted to other hackathons, and each person can join only one team. Participants also receive certificates and sponsor perks.
dates_note: Opening ceremony Friday, January 8, 2027 at 7 PM EST; submissions due Sunday, January 10 at noon EST; closing ceremony 8 PM EST.
eligibility: Students only, ages 13+; companies and professional organizations excluded.
prizes: $13,700+ listed, including $250 first-place cash in general and theme tracks, AirPods 4 for best solo hack and best pitch, and participant perks.
